twin_fact: a justification for flying is on file or not
request: Please book my flight from Paris to Amsterdam on 19 January. My mission order explains why I'm flying rather than taking the train.

trip.purpose: Meetings with rail operators in the Netherlands
trip.air_justification: A particularly heavy schedule: meetings in Amsterdam, Rotterdam and Utrecht on 20 January, set out in the signed mission order

sign_offs.name: Head of unit
sign_offs.subject: MISSION_ORDER
sign_offs.note: Mission order signed: purpose, dates and place of the mission

sign_offs.name: Authorising officer
sign_offs.subject: MISSION_ORDER
sign_offs.note: Mission order signed for the budget: the mission's cost estimate

must_keep.quote: When proposing the practical arrangements of the mission, without prejudice to article 12, paragraph 2, of Annex VII to the Staff Regulations, the mission performers are encouraged to use rail travel for distances up to 550km (37) per travel segment as well as for distances above 550km where it is an efficient alternative to air travel , for example in the case of high-speed and/or night trains . When assessing the financial cost, the greener alternative should be favoured where the price of the rail travel is not more than 40% (38) above the price of a n economy -class (39) plane ticket for the journey or segment, if it remains within the budgetary constraints of the DG . The s ame principle for the cost comparison applies between journeys by train and journeys by car that are not zero- or low- emissions.
must_keep.why: rail encouraged up to 550 km and favoured within 40% of the economy plane ticket

must_keep.quote: Air travel for distances up to 550 km must be appropriately justified (40), and direct flights favoured when available, and within reasonable cost variations (40%). Economy class remains the default option.
must_keep.why: air up to 550 km must be justified; direct flights favoured within 40%; economy the default

must_keep.quote: (40) This includes constraints linked to security reasons or particularly heavy schedules (e.g. multiple meetings in different places).
must_keep.why: footnote 40: justifications include security or particularly heavy schedules

must_keep.quote: As a general rule, you can book air travel: a) in economy class or equivalent, including cases where the ticket in question cannot be exchanged or refunded, at the lowest available rates, taking into account the times of meetings and/or special features of the mission;
must_keep.why: (a) economy, including non-refundable, at the lowest available rates

distractors.quote: These two elements (price variation and distance) may be interpreted in a flexible manner
distractors.why: footnote 38: the 550 km and 40% figures are read flexibly; the cases keep wide margins

design_notes: The rail journey is 505 km and its first-class fare (EUR 109) is 20% above the lowest plane fare, so rail would be favoured (lines 630-636) and air travel up to 550 km must be appropriately justified (line 663). Footnote 40 (lines 693-694) counts particularly heavy schedules with meetings in several places, which is the justification on file. The lowest fare: KLM 18:25 at EUR 91.
